name: LMR50410XDBVR
title: LMR50410 4 V to 36 V, 1 A synchronous buck converter, SOT-23-6
summary: A step-down converter with both power MOSFETs on chip, running from 4 V to 36 V and delivering up to 1 A at an output set from 1 V to 28 V by a resistor divider on FB against a 1 V reference. It switches at a fixed 700 kHz under peak-current-mode control, with compensation and a 1.8 ms soft start built in. One version drops into pulse-frequency mode at light load to save power; the other stays in forced PWM at every load. Protection covers cycle-by-cycle peak and valley current limits, hiccup on a sustained short, input UVLO and thermal shutdown; EN is a precision enable input.
key_figures: 450 mΩ high side, 240 mΩ low side typ
80 µA typ non-switching (PFM version); 3 µA typ shutdown

pins.name: CB
pins.function: Supply for the high-side gate driver. A 100 nF capacitor of good quality goes between CB and SW.

pins.name: GND
pins.function: Power ground; inside, the source of the low-side MOSFET. Joins system ground and the ground ends of CIN and COUT, with the shortest possible path to CIN.

pins.name: FB
pins.function: Feedback input. A divider from the output to FB sets VOUT. FB must not be shorted to ground while the part runs.

pins.name: EN
pins.function: Precision enable: high runs the converter, low stops it. Must not float; may be tied to VIN. A resistor divider from VIN on this pin gives an adjustable input UVLO.

pins.name: VIN
pins.function: Input supply, feeding the internal bias regulator and the high-side MOSFET. The input bypass capacitors connect straight between this pin and GND.

pins.name: SW
pins.function: Switch node: the high-side MOSFET's source and the low-side MOSFET's drain. The power inductor connects to this pin.

circuits.title: Application Circuit, 12 V to 5 V
circuits.description: A 12 V input stepped down to 5 V. CIN decouples VIN to ground, and EN is wired to VIN so the converter starts whenever the input is present. CBOOT, from CB to SW, holds the high-side gate supply. L carries the switch-node current to the output, where COUT filters it. RFBT and RFBB divide VOUT to the 1 V that FB regulates: 88.7 kΩ over 22.1 kΩ gives 5 V.

circuits.title: Simplified Schematic
circuits.description: The minimum part count: an input capacitor at VIN with EN tied to the input, a bootstrap capacitor from CB to SW, the inductor from SW to the output with its output capacitor, and a two-resistor divider from the output to FB. The input may be anything up to 36 V.

operation.text: Both orderable versions switch at 700 kHz and have an adjustable output. LMR50410XDBVR runs in PFM at light load; LMR50410XFDBVR (and its G4 form) is forced PWM at every load. An automotive LMR50410-Q1 exists as a separately qualified version.

Peak-current-mode control at a fixed frequency. The voltage loop sets a peak-current command from the output error; inductor current is sensed in the high-side switch and ends each on-time when it reaches that command. While the high side conducts, SW sits near VIN and the inductor current rises at (VIN – VOUT)/L; after a dead time the low-side switch takes over and the current falls at –VOUT/L. Loop compensation is internal, which keeps the loop stable with a range of output capacitors.

VOUT is set by a divider from the output to FB against the 1.0 V reference. Use 1% resistors with a low temperature coefficient; their tolerance and drift add to the regulation error. RFBB is picked for the divider current and RFBT follows. The suggested RFBT range is 10 kΩ to 100 kΩ. A smaller RFBT pre-loads the output, cutting the VOUT offset in PFM at the cost of very-light-load efficiency; a larger one saves standing current. Above 1 MΩ it is not recommended, because the feedback node picks up noise and its trace needs more care.

The part shuts down with EN below 0.95 V and needs more than 1.36 V to start. EN is an input that must not be left open. Wiring EN to VIN lets the part start by itself once VIN is in range. A divider RENT/RENB from VIN to EN sets a precise input UVLO, useful for sequencing or for a battery discharge cut-off; a logic signal may also drive EN. EN must stay below VIN + 0.3 V, and EN should not be driven while VIN is at 0 V.

operation.topic: Minimum on-time, minimum off-time and frequency foldback
operation.text: The high side cannot be on for less than about 60 ns or off for less than about 110 ns. When either limit is reached the part lowers its switching frequency instead of losing regulation: at high VIN the on-time hits its floor and the frequency drops to reach a lower duty cycle; at low VIN the off-time hits its floor and the frequency drops to stretch the duty cycle, down to about 133 kHz. This widens the input range over which VOUT stays regulated and lowers the effective dropout.

A capacitor from CB to SW powers the high-side gate drive; it is topped up during each low-side conduction interval. The value to use is 0.1 µF, ceramic X7R or X5R, rated 16 V or more. Every design needs it.

Both the peak and the valley inductor current are limited. The high-side current, sensed after a blanking time, is compared each cycle with the error amplifier output less slope compensation and is clamped at ISC. The low-side current is also watched: if it is still above ILS_LIMIT at the end of a cycle, the low side stays on until the current falls below ILS_LIMIT, and only then does the high side turn on again after a dead time. With both limits active the output current is held near (ILS_LIMIT + ISC)/2. If FB falls under 40% of VREF and the low-side limit trips for 256 cycles in a row, the part enters hiccup: it turns off for about 135 ms and then restarts, repeating until the fault clears, which keeps dissipation down during a sustained short. In the FPWM version the inductor current may go negative; once it passes the negative limit the low side turns off and the high side turns on at once.

At enable or power-up the internal reference ramps up over 1.8 ms typ, limiting inrush. For the first 33 ms typ (TOCP_BLK) the overcurrent protection is blanked and the part charges the output by controlling the average inductor current, so a large output capacitance at high VOUT does not trip hiccup and cause repeated restarts.
Above 170 °C junction temperature both FETs stop switching. Once the die cools below 158 °C the part restarts through its soft start.

With VEN below 0.95 V the part is shut down; with VIN under its 3.25 V UVLO threshold the converter is off. With both above their thresholds it is active, in one of four modes set by load: CCM at fixed frequency when the load exceeds half the inductor ripple (both versions, and the mode that supplies the full 1 A with least ripple); DCM at fixed frequency below that (PFM version); PFM at very light load, with the frequency reduced (PFM version); FPWM at fixed frequency down to no load (FPWM version).

Below half the ripple current the low-side switch turns off when the inductor current falls to ILS_ZC, 20 mA typ, giving diode emulation and cutting switching and conduction loss. At lighter load, once either the minimum on-time or the minimum peak current IPEAK_MIN (300 mA typ) is reached, the loop lowers the switching frequency to stay in regulation, saving further switching loss.

The FPWM version stays in PWM at all loads, including no load, by letting the inductor current reverse. It gives up light-load efficiency for small output ripple, tight regulation and a constant frequency.
A higher frequency allows smaller inductors and output capacitors but costs switching loss and heat; the usable frequency is also bounded by the minimum on-time, VIN, VOUT and the foldback limits.

Inductance, saturation current and RMS current are what matter. Size the inductance at the highest VIN, where ripple is largest, with KIND between 0.2 and 0.6. Saturation current must exceed the peak current limit, since RMS and peak currents can be high during an overcurrent event. A smaller inductor gives faster transients, lower DCR and less size, but too much ripple can trip the current limit at full load and raises core loss and output ripple. Under peak current mode a fair amount of ripple helps the current comparator's signal-to-noise ratio.

COUT sets steady-state ripple, loop stability and the overshoot and undershoot on a load step. Ripple has an ESR part and a capacitive part. On a load step the capacitors supply the difference while the loop, which needs eight or more clock cycles, brings the inductor current to the new level; the capacitance must cover the current difference for those 8 cycles within the allowed deviation.

A high-frequency ceramic decoupling capacitor of 2.2 µF or more, X5R or X7R, is needed at the input. Its voltage rating must exceed the highest input voltage; twice the highest input voltage is suggested to allow for ceramic derating. The design example uses one 2.2 µF, 50 V, X7R part (about 10 mΩ ESR, 1 A current rating), plus a 0.1 µF capacitor next to the pins for high-frequency filtering.

The input supply, 4.0 V to 36 V, must be well regulated, carry the full input current and hold its voltage; its source resistance must be low enough that a current step does not pull VIN into a false UVLO trip. A supply more than a few inches away may need bulk capacitance beside the ceramics; 10 µF or 22 µF electrolytic is typical.

Put CIN as close as possible to VIN and GND; it carries the high di/dt pulses and its loop sets most of the radiated EMI. Ground both input and output capacitors through local top-layer copper tied to GND, and place the output capacitors near the inductor's output end. Keep the SW trace to the inductor short and only as wide as the load current needs. Make VIN, VOUT and ground connections wide. Place RFBT and RFBB next to FB, which is high impedance and noise sensitive; the trace from VOUT to the divider may be long, and for accuracy at the load it may sense there, routed away from SW and the inductor, ideally on another layer with ground plane between. Use a mid-layer ground plane for shielding and heat. GND, VIN and SW carry most of the heat, so give them large copper with arrays of vias to inner and bottom ground planes, enough to keep the junction below 125 °C. Keep the bootstrap capacitor close to CB and SW and the SW area small.
